sector_notes: The latest U.S. session was strongly risk-off: the Nasdaq fell 2.84% on October 30 and the S&P 500 fell 1.80% as AI-spending and technology-earnings concerns intensified. Energy and several non-technology groups showed better relative resilience, while healthcare, consumer defensives, financials and selected industrials offer cleaner diversification. The coming week adds U.S. midterm-election uncertainty and a heavy macro/earnings calendar, so the preferred stance is selective momentum rather than aggressive technology exposure.
